title: Point sections compute lisse ranks and detect finite-stage constructible vanishing
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite subextension of $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $F\in\Sh_c(T,E)$ [def-weil-constructible-heart], use completed derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and use the specified continuous realization $J_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] and point functor $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], where $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For a reduced locally closed immersion $b:C\hookrightarrow T$ with $C$ nonempty and connected and $J_C(Lb^*F)$ lisse of constant finite rank $r$, every $k$-point $x:s\to C$ has a natural identification
$$\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(L(bx)^*F)\cong\Gamma(s,x^*J_C(Lb^*F)),$$
and this vector space has dimension $r$. Here lisse means pro-etale locally a finite free module over the continuous coefficient ring; no global basis on $C$ is assumed. In particular, vanishing of this vector space at one such point implies $Lb^*F=0$. For the whole scheme, if $\operatorname{Fib}_{s,E}(Ly^*F)=0$ for every $k$-rational point $y:s\to T$, then $F=0$. This includes $T=\varnothing$ and rank zero, and is restricted to constructible rational adic objects; it asserts no point-conservativity for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: §6.8, Definition 6.8.3 and Proposition 6.8.14(2); rank computation by split covers of Spec k, then finite open–closed devissage (returned proof Steps 7–8).

proof.text: Put $K=Lb^*F$ and $L=J_C(K)$. The hypothesis places $L$ in degree zero. By the equivalence and pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization], $J_s(L(bx)^*F)\cong Lx_c^*L$. A finite locally free module is flat, so its derived pullback is its ordinary module pullback $x^*L$. The sections-localization isomorphism of [lem-tw-lisse-point-sections-realization], applied to an integral representative of $L(bx)^*F$ on $s$, identifies its prescribed rational fibre with $\Gamma(s,J_s(L(bx)^*F))$. Combining gives the asserted identification with $\Gamma(s,x^*L)$. It is natural because both cited comparisons are natural; no basis has been chosen.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit assembly with Stacks 09AB and 09AH.

proof.text: Pull a pro-etale cover trivializing $L$ back along $x$. It trivializes $x^*L$ with rank $r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-field-proetale-evaluation], this cover of $s$ has a section through some member. Pulling that member's trivialization back along the section gives $x^*L\cong(E_s^c)^{\oplus r}$. The continuous-function description in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] gives $E_s^c(s)=C(\{*\},E)=E$. Consequently sections give $E^r$, of dimension $r$, including $r=0$. This trivialization is used only to compute dimension, not to define the natural identification in Step 1. If the fibre vanishes, $r=0$; then the original cover of $C$ trivializes $L$ as zero. For any section over any site object its restrictions are zero on this cover, so the separatedness axiom makes the section zero. Thus $L=0$ and the equivalence $J_C$ reflects zero, giving $Lb^*F=0$.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit assembly with Stacks 09AB and 09AH.

proof.text: For the global assertion, [lem-dl-a1-heart-connected-lisse-strata] makes $M=J_T(F)$ a sheaf in degree zero and supplies a finite good stratification by reduced locally closed strata, with finitely many connected components and a $k$-point on each nonempty component. For each such component $b:C\hookrightarrow T$, choose its supplied point $x$. The hypothesis at $y=bx$ and Step 2 give $Lb^*F=0$. The pullback comparison in that stratification statement identifies the restriction of $M$ to $C$ with zero. Hence its restriction to each stratum is zero: restrictions to the open connected components detect sections by the sheaf axiom. No point-detection assertion for unrestricted pro-etale sheaves is used.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit assembly with Stacks 09AB and 09AH.

proof.text: First reduce the ambient scheme to $T_{\mathrm{red}}$: [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] and [lem-trf-proetale-topological-invariance] make inverse image an equivalence of pro-etale topoi, so it detects zero also on module sheaves by applying the equivalence to their underlying sheaves and actions. The ring identification and its compatibility with composition are [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. The inverse image of $M$ has the same zero restrictions to the reduced strata. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $T$ is Noetherian (a field is Noetherian), hence every open encountered below is quasi-compact. All reduced closed subschemes encountered are again separated finite type over $k$.

source.place: Examples 4.1.10 and 4.2.11; Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; explicit assembly with Stacks 09AB and 09AH.

proof.text: On a reduced scheme with this finite good stratification, induct on the number of nonempty strata to show that a module sheaf with zero restrictions to all strata is zero. With none, the scheme is empty and the empty-cover sheaf axiom gives the zero sheaf. Otherwise choose an open stratum $U$ and let $Z$ be the reduced closed complement. Such an open stratum exists: order the finitely many strata by containment in their closures; the frontier condition makes the complement of a maximal stratum the finite union of the closures of the other strata, hence closed. The induced stratification on $Z$ is good and has fewer strata. Its restrictions are zero by composition of inverse images, so induction gives $i^{-1}M=0$; also $j^{-1}M=0$ on $U$. The module open–closed sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applicable because $j$ is quasi-compact, reads $0\to j_!0\to M\to i_*0\to0$, hence $M=0$. The same ring-identifications of Step 4 identify these inverse images with the zero restrictions already proved. Returning from the reduction gives $J_T(F)=0$, and the equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] gives $F=0$.

tool_uses.why: Continuous coefficient realization equivalence and natural pullback/composition comparisons; this is coefficient infrastructure, not the unit weight-gap argument.
Canonical sections-localization isomorphism at the point for every integral representative; the unit has no alternative point normalization.
Every cover of the algebraically closed point splits, so finite local freeness computes dimension.
Reduction is a universal homeomorphism, needed for the reduced stratification.
Inverse image along the reduction detects zero; no weight argument is replaced.
Identifies coefficient rings under the reduced locally closed restrictions used in devissage.
Ensures all open complements in finite devissage are quasi-compact.
Generic module-sheaf open–closed exact sequence assembles zero restrictions.
